bullets.title: Fed pricing: 25bp hike near-certainty as core PCE holds at 0.3% m/m; GDP revised sharply higher
bullets.body: October core PCE came in at +0.3% m/m in line with consensus, but annual core accelerated to 3.3%. Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3% SAAR from the 3.4% flash estimate, with consumer spending revised up to 4.2%. Markets are pricing a 25bp Fed hike as near-certainty at 92% per FedWatch, and hawkish Fed/tightening financial conditions are cited as the primary market overhang.

bullets.title: Global core inflation stuck at 3.4%; tech CPI flipped positive on AI-related memory price increases
bullets.body: JPM's global inflation monitor shows core inflation firm at 3.4% (3m saar), with US supercore at 5.5%. Notably, the tech CPI proxy shifted from subtracting 0.1pp to adding 0.3pp to core in October due to AI-related memory and tech price increases. Further Brent declines to $75-80/bbl could lower global inflation from 4.4%ar in 4Q26 to 2-2.5%ar in 1H27, but food inflation is accelerating to 3.4%ar with peak impacts expected 1Q27.

bullets.title: HF deleveraging ~30% complete; semis at +4z short — setup for reversal if volatility recedes
bullets.body: JPM positioning data shows HF net exposure declined >30% from 12-month highs, comparable to late 2018 and March 2020. US semis saw 3-sigma net selling over 20 days with shorts at +4z, potentially setting the stage for a reversal. CTAs are broadly neutral US equities at the 20th percentile (not yet at Apr 2025 extreme bearishness), and APAC flows turned +1.6z net buying WoW. SPX historically gains 3.2% avg rest of Q4 from comparable November points (82% hit rate), though 2007 drawdown path is cited as the most similar analog.

bullets.title: JPM: AI stock capitulation underway — Dec/Jan recovery expected as year-end re-entry begins
bullets.body: JPM flows analysis argues HF and active managers abandoned AI stocks in Oct/Nov for profit-taking rather than valuation concerns, with quant CTAs building their largest short positions in tech indices since Liberation Day. Market depth and breadth collapsed to capitulation-phase levels. Recovery in AI stocks is expected Dec/Jan as year-end traders re-enter. Bitcoin ETF outflows intensified with IBIT outflow pace faster than May-June 2026, and MicroStrategy's premium to NAV collapsed to a record low of 0.88.

bullets.title: Wolfe: All-SaaS index -7.3% WoW; SOX -10% past week despite Jensen commentary
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index is trading at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales and fell 7.31% week-over-week. The SOX index dropped 10% over the past week despite positive Jensen Huang commentary. The path of least resistance is described as still lower, with funding/cost-of-capital constraints, peak capex/earnings growth uncertainty, and monetization questions dominating over seasonality as the key bullish argument.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang to testify before Senate on AI export controls Dec 1-3
bullets.body: Jensen Huang is scheduled for a House transcribed interview Dec 1 and Senate Banking Committee testimony Dec 3 (hearing titled 'Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of US Export Controls'). NVDA's General Counsel Tim Teter will appear before House Foreign Affairs, the Select Committee on CCP, and House Intelligence Committee on Dec 2. This is a significant policy catalyst to watch for NVDA and the broader AI/semi complex.

bullets.title: US export curbs flood GPU resale market: ByteDance deployed ~36k B200s in Malaysia before restrictions
bullets.body: Since the Nov 16 BIS interim final rule restricting Chinese remote access to chips in third-party data centers, an unusually high number of advanced NVIDIA GPUs have come to market from resellers. The rule adds license requirements for advanced semis to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. ByteDance had reportedly deployed ~$2.5B worth of B200 chips (~36k units) in Malaysia before restrictions took effect.

bullets.title: UBS: Semi stocks pricing ~25-30% cuts to 2028 compute capacity on power constraints
bullets.body: UBS argues the market is discounting nearly all of the 'powered shell gap' in semiconductor valuations, with stocks pricing in roughly 25-30% cuts to 2028 datacenter compute capacity. UBS is cutting its own datacenter capacity estimates across coverage but notes valuations have become attractive as a result. This is a key framing for the semi selloff.

bullets.title: JPM Asia 2027 outlook: AI supercycle intact; bearish 'overbuilt capex' narrative called stale
bullets.body: JPM argues AI stocks represent >50% of the Asia index weight and should drive ~70% of 2027 earnings growth. Datacenter projects are generating ROI well over 30% at current rental rates, and classic cycle-peak signals (inventory builds, lead-time shortening, rapid capacity ramp) are largely absent. The base case MXASJ target is 1200 (bull 1500, bear 900) on $115 EPS, with overweight allocations in Taiwan, Korea, and HK tech.

bullets.title: Brent climbed to $94/bbl on Middle East tanker attacks; US vehicle activity -1.8% YoY
bullets.body: JPM's Energy Shock Monitor shows Brent stabilized around $91/bbl before climbing past $94 on Middle East tanker attack news. US vehicle activity is running 1.8% below 2025 levels while China is down 2.5% YoY. Natural gas markets are diverging — European TTF rose week-over-week while US Henry Hub fell. Chase Card data shows solid +0.4% m/m nominal control retail sales gain in November.

bullets.title: Sector rotation: RTY outperforms, Mag 7 lags; homebuilders and energy lead, semis/airlines weak
bullets.body: Into the close, RTY futures led SPX and NDX with Mag 7 underperforming all three indices. Within the SPX, materials and homebuilders outperformed while tech and semis lagged. NDX expected to settle 25,800-26,200 and SPX 7,150-7,230. Discretionary sector was +4.5% for the week vs S&P +3.9%; staples lagged at +2.0%.

bullets.title: Global bond supply-demand improves $0.4tr in 2027; JPM sees ~20bp yield decline ahead
bullets.body: JPM projects global bond supply to decline ~$0.6tr in 2027 as a larger share of the US deficit is funded via T-bills, improving the demand-supply balance by ~$0.4tr and implying ~20bp decline in Global Agg yields. Retail investors are projected to maintain strong $1.3tr net bond demand (down modestly from $1.5tr in 2026) while G4 central bank demand deteriorates slightly to -$1.0tr.

bullets.title: CRWD acquired ZS in largest-ever security deal; Wolfe sees stronger AI security positioning despite selloff
bullets.body: CrowdStrike acquired Zscaler in what Wolfe Research calls the largest security deal in history. Despite near-term share price weakness, Wolfe sees the combined entity as better positioned for AI security market share. RBRK checks are strong with positive financial setup, and OKTA is showing cRPO acceleration in F3Q with AI momentum early but progressing.

bullets.title: Holiday consumer electronics demand resilient; smartphones and gaming lead at 51% and 44% intent
bullets.body: Citi's holiday survey shows US consumer electronics spending flat YoY but concentrated: smartphones rank #1 at 51% purchase intent (iPhone and Samsung Galaxy tied at 42% each), gaming peripherals rank #2 at 44% — surpassing TVs. AR/VR headsets generate ~16% demand supportive for Meta. AI-driven replacement cycle is cited as a tailwind for Apple and Samsung.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley bullish on 2027 M&A activity; expects record deal volumes before 2028 regulatory window narrows
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley expects 2027 M&A to reach record volumes driven by equity market gains and a narrowing regulatory window ahead of 2028. Deutsche Bank separately sees equity tokenization and 24/7 trading as multi-year structural market catalysts.

bullets.title: US hotel RevPAR +13.4% YoY for week ending Nov 21; Las Vegas +34%, all chain scales positive
bullets.body: Weekly US RevPAR grew +13.4% YoY (ADR +7.3%, occupancy +336bps), consistent with the prior week's +12.9%. The largest 25 markets rose +14.5% YoY led by Las Vegas +34.2% and Chicago +28.9%. Trailing 28-day RevPAR is up +10.0% YoY; 4Q26 YTD tracking at +9.3%. C-Corp (HLT, MAR) and REIT operators (HST, PK) are both outperforming consensus expectations.

bullets.title: November auto SAAR est. 15.6mn; luxury demand improving on incentives, BEV mix ticking higher
bullets.body: JPM estimates November US light vehicle SAAR at ~15.6mn, a modest sequential improvement from 15.5mn in October, constrained by election uncertainty, capital markets volatility, and holiday calendar. Luxury segment is showing near-term improvement after ~6 months of muted trends on higher OEM incentive spending (~+$300/unit m/m to ~$3,800/unit). BEV penetration is tracking modestly higher sequentially vs. 6.3% in October.

bullets.title: PANW faces accounting fraud lawsuit from former regional VP alleging revenue misrepresentation
bullets.body: A former Palo Alto Networks regional VP filed suit alleging the company misrepresented deals as booked revenues to boost earnings. This is a headline risk for PANW as it navigates the broader cyber sector selloff following the CRWD-ZS deal.

bullets.title: GLP-1 adoption could reduce restaurant industry sales 0.5-0.7% by 2030; 73% of users cut fast-food visits
bullets.body: KeyBanc notes 90% of GLP-1 users eat less per sitting and 73% have reduced fast-food visits, with Technomic estimating 0.5-0.7% industry sales headwind by 2030. Circana data shows foodservice spending declines through the first year of GLP-1 use with moderate recovery in year two. This is a secular headwind for the restaurant sector.

bullets.title: Fed Beige Book: 8 of 12 districts saw slight-to-moderate growth; consumer spending flat with price sensitivity rising
bullets.body: The Fed's Beige Book showed 8 of 12 districts experienced slight-to-moderate growth. Consumer spending was flat with heightened price sensitivity noted across districts. Jobless claims printed at 189K, well below the 200K consensus, adding to the case for continued Fed tightening.
